label: Personality
value: Anne is highly imaginative.
unit: Anne is highly imaginative, romantic, and ambitious, possessing a deep love for beauty and nature. She is passionate and impulsive, often plunging high into enthusiasm before crashing into despair or making hasty choices without thinking. She is intensely loyal and affectionate toward her true friends, holding high ideals while keeping a pure, transparent, and unselfish nature. Strongly opposed to harsh punishments and unfairness, she displays a real knack for nurturing children and winning over those around her.

label: History
value: Anne was orphaned in Bolingbroke.
unit: After being orphaned in Bolingbroke, Anne spent a hard early childhood working for foster families and living in an asylum before being adopted by Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert at Green Gables. She quickly made Avonlea her beloved home, excelling at school and competing passionately in academic rivalries with Gilbert Blythe. After completing a year at Queen's Academy and winning the Avery Scholarship, she chose to stay in Avonlea as a teacher to support Marilla following Matthew's death. During her time teaching, she co-founded the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and served as its secretary. Upon completing her two years of teaching, she enrolled at Redmond College in Kingsport alongside close friends Priscilla Grant and Gilbert Blythe. At Redmond, Anne flourished socially and academically, eventually moving into Patty's Place with her chums, and dedicating herself to winning the Thorburn Scholarship in English.

She quickly made Avonlea her beloved home, excelling at school and competing passionately in academic rivalries with Gilbert Blythe. After completing a year at Queen's Academy and winning the Avery Scholarship, she chose to stay in Avonlea as a teacher to support Marilla following Matthew's death. During her time teaching, she co-founded the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and served as its secretary. Upon completing her two years of teaching, she enrolled at Redmond College in Kingsport alongside close friends Priscilla Grant and Gilbert Blythe. At Redmond, Anne flourished socially and academically, eventually moving into Patty's Place with her chums, and dedicating herself to winning the Thorburn Scholarship in English.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye was taken in as an orphan.
unit: Anthony Pye was taken in as an orphan nephew by Mrs. George Pye and her husband. Upon moving to Avonlea, he began attending the local school taught by Anne Shirley. He immediately took a dislike to Anne, maintaining that she was no good like all female teachers. During his school days, he engaged in pranks, such as pouring slate-bottle water down Aurelia Clay's neck and placing a live mouse in Anne's desk drawer. After remaining unaffected by Anne's lectures about being a gentleman, his defiance eventually cracked when Anne punished him with a pointer, causing his bravado to fail and bringing tears to his eyes.

value: Aunt Jamesina is sweet

Though she loves the young women under her care deeply, she admits she does not always fully understand them.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina was named after James.
unit: Aunt Jamesina was named after her father James, who drowned at sea a month before she was born. In her youth, she desired a yellow silk dress, but neither her mother nor her husband permitted her to have one. She raised a daughter named Elizabeth, whom she taught to cook before she attended college; Elizabeth eventually married and went to India as a foreign missionary, a path Aunt Jamesina had prayed for despite worrying about the snakes there. Left alone in a large house, Aunt Jamesina accepted an invitation to move to Kingsport to keep house for a group of college students—including Anne Shirley, Stella, Priscilla, and Phil Gordon—at Patty's Place. She brought along her grey-and-white cat, the Sarah-cat, and took charge of the household and its pets, including Joseph and Rusty. Over three college winters, she served as a beloved housemother to the young women. At the end of their studies, she decided to take Rusty home with her alongside Joseph and the Sarah-cat.

value: Billy drove Anne Shirley to a concert in White Sands.
unit: Billy drove Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and his sister Jane Andrews to a concert in White Sands in their double-seated buggy. Following the concert, he ran off out of mortal fear of being invited to the social supper inside, but waited outside with the team to drive the girls back home. Later, after his father gave him the upper farm in his own name, Billy wished to marry Anne Shirley. Due to his extreme shyness, he badgered his sister Jane into proposing to Anne on his behalf, offering to wait until Anne finished college if necessary. After Anne declined the proposal, Billy did not break his heart and instead married Nettie Blewett, whom his mother favored as a good manager. They made their official married appearance together at the Avonlea church.

label: History
value: Leonora Bowman was taken in by Miss Lavendar Lewis.
unit: Leonora Bowman was taken in by Miss Lavendar Lewis at the age of fourteen to live at Echo Lodge for board and clothes. Because her three older sisters—Charlotta, Julietta, and Evelina—had previously served as Miss Lavendar's handmaidens, Miss Lavendar dubbed her 'Charlotta the Fourth'. She proved to be the best and most understanding of the Bowman girls, keeping her mistress's secrets and welcoming guests like Anne Shirley and Diana Barry with open arms. She helped energetically with the garden, sewing, and house preparations leading up to Miss Lavendar's wedding to Stephen Irving. After the marriage, she moved with the Irvings to Boston, where she suffered from severe homesickness. She returned with the family to Echo Lodge during subsequent summers, having grown into a fashionable young lady who maintained a fond friendship with Anne.

label: History
value: Davy Keith and Dora are twins.
unit: Davy Keith and his twin sister Dora were orphaned after their mother's death and taken in at Green Gables by Marilla Cuthbert and Anne Shirley. Initially unruly and full of constant mischief, Davy quickly developed a deep affection for Anne while clashing with the strict rules of Marilla and Mrs. Rachel Lynde. He enrolled in the local school alongside his sister, sharing a desk with Milty Boulter, and over time he gradually reformed into a better-behaved child. During Anne's absence at Redmond College, he kept in touch by sending letters, helped around the farm, and competed with Milty Boulter over his growth.

label: History
value: Diana Barry grew up at Orchard Slope
unit: Diana Barry grew up at Orchard Slope in Avonlea. As a child, she met Anne Shirley and the two swore a solemn, lifelong oath of bosom friendship over imaginary running water. Though briefly separated when her mother forbade their companionship after an accidental intoxication incident, the friendship was restored after Diana sought Anne's assistance during her sister Minnie May's severe attack of croup. Diana actively participated in childhood pastimes, including the Story Club and local performances. When older, she joined the Avonlea Village Improvement Society as its treasurer. She did not pursue higher education at Queen's Academy or Redmond College, remaining in Avonlea while her friends moved away. Diana became engaged to Fred Wright at eighteen, and the two later married at Orchard Slope. Following their wedding, she gave birth to their first child, a son named Fred.

label: History
value: Gilbert spent three years in Alberta
unit: After spending three years in Alberta with his sick father, Gilbert returned to Avonlea to resume his schooling. He quickly established a fierce academic rivalry with Anne Shirley that lasted through their school years and their time at Queen's Academy, where he won the medal in their graduating class. Although he originally applied for the Avonlea school teaching post, he surrendered it to Anne so she could stay near Green Gables, taking a position at White Sands instead to save money for college. During his time teaching, he co-founded the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and served as its president. He later attended Redmond College alongside Anne, leading the Freshmen to victory in the Arts Rush, becoming class president, and captaining the football team. Gilbert proposed to Anne in their second year at Redmond, but she refused him, leading to a period of distant courtesy between them. Following his graduation with High Honors and the Cooper Prize, he suffered a near-fatal attack of typhoid fever. Upon receiving word via Phil Gordon that Anne did not care for Roy Gardner, he recovered quickly and proposed to Anne a second time, which she joyfully accepted.

label: Quotes
value: > And I suppose you were scared to death to come here and tell me, after the fuss I made yesterday, hey? But you mustn’t mind me, I’m a terrible outspoken old fellow, that’s all . . . awful apt to tell the truth, no matter if it is a bit plain.

label: Quotes
value: > I guess you’ve got a spice of temper, It goes with hair like yours, I reckon. Avonlea is a pretty decent place or I wouldn’t have located here; but I suppose even you will admit that it has some faults?

label: Quotes
value: > That old nuisance of a Rachel Lynde was here again today, pestering me for a subscription towards buying a carpet for the vestry room, I detest that woman more than anybody I know. She can put a whole sermon, text, comment, and application, into six words, and throw it at you like a brick.

label: Quotes
value: > Well, we’re going to miss you an awful lot, Emily and me. To be sure, Mrs. Lynde’ll be over there in your place. There ain’t nobody but a substitute can be found for them.

label: Quotes
value: > I daresay there’s been many a romance in Avonlea—and many a tragedy, too, But your folks ain’t like real folks anywhere. They talk too much and use too high-flown language. There’s one place where that Dalrymple chap talks even on for two pages, and never lets the girl get a word in edgewise. If he’d done that in real life she’d have pitched him.

value: In early April, Mr. Harrison bought Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea
unit: In early April, Mr. Harrison bought Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea and moved from Scottsford, New Brunswick. Living alone with a swearing parrot named Ginger and keeping no fixed meal schedules, he quickly gained a local reputation as an eccentric crank. His friendship with Anne Shirley began tumultuously when he flew into a rage over her stray Jersey cow, but the two soon became warm neighbors who frequently confided in each other. He hired young John Henry Carter to help around the farm, though the boy complained of irregular meals. Later, Mr. Harrison's estranged wife Emily unexpectedly rejoined him in Avonlea following the death of Ginger, leading him to shave, tidy up his house, attend church every Sunday, and become even friendlier. During Anne's college years, he served as a brutally honest critic of her writing, encouraging her to cut excessive descriptions and high-flown dialogue.

value: Jane is sensible.
unit: Jane is sensible, practical, composed, and conscientious. She is steady and unflappable, possessing steady nerves that do not rattle under pressure during examinations. Unpoetical by nature, she approaches work with a straightforward, plodding manner. Although ladylike and well-behaved, she believes a teacher must be a little cross to maintain order in the classroom.

label: History
value: Jane grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Jane grew up in Avonlea, attending the local school and participating in a childhood Story Club with her friends Anne, Diana, and Ruby. During a school picnic, she was saved from drowning in the Lake of Shining Waters by her father when she leaned out too far. She later joined the Queen's Academy preparation class, passed the Entrance examinations with steady composure, and pursued Second Class teacher's certification, taking top honors in the domestic science course. Upon graduating, she secured a position teaching school at Newbridge, where her work earned her a place on the Inspector's Roll of Honor. Active in community life, Jane served as the chairman of the re-shingling and painting committee for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. After teaching at Newbridge, she accepted a teaching post in Avonlea before moving to teach on the western prairies. Prior to her departure for the West, she carried out a proposal of marriage to Anne on behalf of her shy brother Billy, which Anne declined. After returning home from the West, Jane married Mr. Inglis, a Winnipeg millionaire, in a splendid ceremony and went on a wedding tour to Europe.

label: History
value: Josie attended Avonlea school
unit: Josie attended Avonlea school under Mr. Phillips and later Miss Stacy. During her school days, she was caught peeping in her book during a spelling exercise by Anne Shirley. At a gathering, she successfully walked the top of the Barry garden board fence after performing a dare, triumphing over the other girls. She caused friction among her classmates when she became sulky over not getting the role of the fairy queen in a local concert dialogue, and later stopped speaking with Julia Bell for three months after making a derogatory comment about Julia's recitation bow. At the Exhibition, Josie earned first prize for her knitted lace. She eventually joined the Queen's class to study for college, noting that she was pursuing higher education purely for education's sake rather than out of financial necessity. While at Queen's Academy, she maintained a reputation as the sharpest-tongued student. When Anne Shirley's prize story was published later on, Josie spitefully claimed that Anne had merely copied it from an old paper.

label: History
value: Miss Lavendar Lewis lived a quiet life.
unit: Miss Lavendar Lewis lived a quiet life at Echo Lodge in Grafton. In her youth, she was engaged to Stephen Irving, but after a silly quarrel fueled by pride on both sides, he left for the States, breaking her heart. Ten years prior to meeting Anne Shirley, her mother passed away, leading her to hire a series of young girls named Charlotta to keep her company, ending with Charlotta the Fourth. She befriended Anne Shirley and Diana Barry when they visited Echo Lodge, finding a kindred spirit in Anne. Through Anne's connection with Stephen's son Paul, Stephen Irving learned she was unmarried and returned to reconcile with her. The two were married in the honeysuckle arbor at Echo Lodge and subsequently relocated to Boston.

label: Personality
value: Marilla is a practical woman.
unit: Marilla is a practical, sensible, and self-contained woman with a rigid conscience and strict moral discipline. Though she is brusque, stoic, and sometimes sarcastic—especially when suffering from headaches—she possesses a hidden sense of humor and a deep capacity for tenderness. She is deeply devoted to her duties and hesitates to display open emotion or pride, though over time she mellows into a much milder and more forgiving guardian.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables in Avonlea with his sister Marilla. Because of his aging health and the difficulty of finding hired farm help, he and Marilla arranged to adopt a young orphan boy from Hopeton. When Matthew drove to Bright River station to collect the child, he was met instead by Anne Shirley. Despite his extreme fear of little girls, Matthew was captivated by her talkative nature and silently resolved that they should keep her. Through his gentle persistency, he convinced Marilla to let Anne remain at Green Gables. Over the following years, Matthew formed a deep bond with Anne, acting as a sympathetic confidant and frequently spoiling her with gifts such as a fashionably made dress for a school concert. He encouraged her studies and romantic spirit while suffering from increasingly frequent heart spells. Matthew died instantly of a sudden heart stroke upon reading a newspaper account of the failure of the Abbey Bank.

When Matthew drove to Bright River station to collect the child, he was met instead by Anne Shirley. Despite his extreme fear of little girls, Matthew was captivated by her talkative nature and silently resolved that they should keep her. Through his gentle persistency, he convinced Marilla to let Anne remain at Green Gables. Over the following years, Matthew formed a deep bond with Anne, acting as a sympathetic confidant and frequently spoiling her with gifts such as a fashionably made dress for a school concert. He encouraged her studies and romantic spirit while suffering from increasingly frequent heart spells. Matthew died instantly of a sudden heart stroke upon reading a newspaper account of the failure of the Abbey Bank.

label: History
value: Paul Irving moved from Boston to Avonlea.
unit: Paul Irving moved from Boston to Avonlea to reside with his grandmother, becoming a student under Anne Shirley at Avonlea school. He and Anne quickly became kindred spirits and fast friends. Paul engaged in a drawn battle with St. Clair Donnell over their respective national flags and accidentally fell into a spring while demonstrating that his hair was naturally curly to his crush, Gracie Andrews. His father, Stephen Irving, later surprised him with a visit, during which Stephen reunited with his former love, Lavendar Lewis. After Stephen and Lavendar married, Paul moved with them to Boston, referring to Lavendar as 'Mother Lavendar'. Over the years, Paul grew up, developed an interest in football, and maintained his close bond with Anne.

Paul engaged in a drawn battle with St. Clair Donnell over their respective national flags and accidentally fell into a spring while demonstrating that his hair was naturally curly to his crush, Gracie Andrews. His father, Stephen Irving, later surprised him with a visit, during which Stephen reunited with his former love, Lavendar Lewis. After Stephen and Lavendar married, Paul moved with them to Boston, referring to Lavendar as 'Mother Lavendar'. Over the years, Paul grew up, developed an interest in football, and maintained his close bond with Anne.

label: History
value: Philippa Gordon enters Redmond College as a Freshman.
unit: Philippa Gordon enters Redmond College as a Freshman, quickly becoming a popular student, class beauty, and belle due to her charm and family background. She introduces Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant into Redmond's social life, and the three compete for top academic honors along with Gilbert Blythe. For a long time, she is indecisive between her two hometown suitors, Alec and Alonzo. In her second year, she moves into Patty's Place with Anne, Priscilla, Stella Maynard, and Aunt Jamesina. While spending time at Prospect Point, she meets Jonas Blake, a Redmond graduate, falls in love with him, and eventually becomes engaged to him. She devotes herself to studying mathematics in her final year, successfully overcoming her mother's objections to marrying a minister. Following graduation, she marries Jonas in Bolingbroke with Anne serving as her bridesmaid.

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster in Avonlea.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster in Avonlea, boarding at Eben Wright's house near the schoolhouse. During his time teaching, he frequently spent his attention on the older students preparing for Queen's, such as Prissy Andrews, while neglecting the younger scholars. His lack of strict discipline led to poor room order and frequent punishments, including whipping Sam Boulter—which led to an altercation with Sam's father—and publicly mortifying and punishing Anne Shirley. During a Mayflower picking outing, he gave all the flowers he found to Prissy Andrews, quoting poetry to her.

label: History
value: Priscilla studied at Queen's Academy.
unit: Priscilla studied at Queen's Academy, where she became close friends with Anne Shirley and Stella Maynard. After graduating, she taught school at Carmody before taking over her own home school on the Island. She participated in the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, contributing a paper on cemeteries. Later, after obtaining her father's consent, she enrolled at Redmond College in Kingsport alongside Anne. Together with Anne, Stella, and Philippa Gordon, she lived at Patty's Place under the chaperonage of Aunt Jamesina. During her college years, she devoted herself to classics, spent a summer visiting Anne in Avonlea, and completed her final Senior examinations at Redmond.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde spent forty-five years living at Lynde's Hollow near Green Gables
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde spent forty-five years living at Lynde's Hollow near Green Gables with her meek husband, Thomas. She was an indispensable force in Avonlea, actively running church societies, participating in local politics, and managing her home and neighbors' affairs. When Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert adopted Anne Shirley, Rachel initially voiced sharp criticism regarding Anne's looks, sparking a temporary quarrel, though she quickly accepted Anne's apology and grew fond of her. At the local Exhibition, she won first prize for her butter and cheese. When her husband Thomas fell ill and passed away, it was revealed that their farm was mortgaged to support their youngest son; consequently, the farm was sold. Following her husband's death, Rachel accepted Marilla's invitation to move into Green Gables, residing in the spare room. At Green Gables, she helped manage the household, assisted in raising the twins Davy and Dora, and remained deeply involved in community and church matters.

She was an indispensable force in Avonlea, actively running church societies, participating in local politics, and managing her home and neighbors' affairs. When Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert adopted Anne Shirley, Rachel initially voiced sharp criticism regarding Anne's looks, sparking a temporary quarrel, though she quickly accepted Anne's apology and grew fond of her. At the local Exhibition, she won first prize for her butter and cheese. When her husband Thomas fell ill and passed away, it was revealed that their farm was mortgaged to support their youngest son; consequently, the farm was sold. Following her husband's death, Rachel accepted Marilla's invitation to move into Green Gables, residing in the spare room. At Green Gables, she helped manage the household, assisted in raising the twins Davy and Dora, and remained deeply involved in community and church matters.

value: Jonas Blake graduated from Redmond College
unit: Jonas Blake graduated from Redmond College and spent time in St. Columbia as a theological student. During one summer, he took charge of the Point Prospect Mission Church, where he met Philippa Gordon and spent his leisure time fishing, boating, and walking on the sands with her. He frequently traveled from St. Columbia to visit Patty's Place, where he became a favorite guest. Although he missed social engagements to lead prayer meetings in the slums, he eventually proposed to Phil Gordon and was accepted. After meeting Phil's family at Mount Holly and winning their affection, they were married the following June.

label: History
value: Roy Gardner belonged to one of the wealthiest families in Kingsport.
unit: Roy Gardner belonged to one of the wealthiest and most prominent families in Kingsport. Two years prior to returning to Redmond, he had to leave his college class to travel abroad with his mother when her health failed. Upon returning, he actively courted Anne Shirley, sending her white orchids, boxes of violets accompanied by poetical sonnets, and writing exquisite letters twice a week. He regularly escorted her to social functions and visited Patty's Place, where Aunt Jamesina and her friends grew fond of him. After Anne graduated from Redmond, Roy took her out and proposed marriage to her, but she turned him down.

label: History
value: Ruby grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Ruby grew up in Avonlea among a large family of sisters. As a child, she attended Avonlea school alongside Anne Shirley and Diana Barry, participating in recitations, concerts, and their private Story Club. After preparing for the Entrance examinations, she attended Queen's Academy to earn a teaching certificate. Upon graduating, she took over the Carmody schoolhouse and spent her leisure time flirting with numerous local admirers. She was rumored to be courted by the Spencervale schoolteacher and received proposals from suitors like Nelson Atkins, whom she rejected after learning his declaration came straight from an etiquette guide. Eventually, she contracted galloping consumption during the winter and stopped teaching, though she maintained that she was getting better and planned to teach at White Sands. She died peacefully in her sleep at home shortly before Jane Andrews departed for the West.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy is hired as the schoolteacher in Avonlea.
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy is hired as the schoolteacher in Avonlea, becoming the town's first female teacher. She introduces physical culture exercises, biweekly recitation afternoons, and outdoor field days to study nature. She establishes a deep rapport with her students and forms the Queen's class to thoroughly prepare advanced pupils for the Entrance examinations. When Anne Shirley is caught reading a novel during class time, Miss Stacy counsels her privately on honesty and time management, winning Anne's deep devotion. After guiding her Queen's class students through their successful Entrance examinations, she concludes her term of teaching in Avonlea. She later returns for visits to Avonlea, during which she attends social gatherings such as a dinner with guests including Mr. and Mrs. Allan.
